script.base: Morning-of-kickoff read, weeks 1-2 only. The close (nflverse games.csv) has Chicago +1.5 and a 49.5 total, so the book expects Dallas to lead by a field goal or less and both teams to score: favorite DAL (49.5+1.5)/2 = 25.5, dog CHI (49.5-1.5)/2 = 24.0. That is a competitive, relatively high-play game, not a blowout and not a 3.5-point dog-throws script. Pace should support both passing games. Dallas's base lean is still Lamb-first through the air (24 targets, 222 yards, 303 air yards in two games) with Ferguson as the second look (18 targets, 101 yards, 112 air) and Javonte Williams as the lead runner (33 carries, 151 yards, about 16.5 carries and 75.5 rush yards a game) without a garbage-time benching. Chicago's base lean is Odunze-first (20 targets, 165 yards, 255 air) with Swift, if he plays through a questionable quad, as the lead back (29 carries, 116 yards). Neither starter group is projected into a snap-risk blowout at a 1.5 spread.
script.flip1: Dallas jumps ahead by two scores. Chicago, the home dog, abandons the run, so Swift (already Questionable, 29 carries / 116 yards) and Monangai (7 carries / 28 yards) lose carries, and Caleb Williams throws more at a Dallas secondary missing DaRon Bland. Dallas then runs the clock with Javonte, which is how a Lamb/Ferguson yardage line can stall late even if the first half was fine. The 1.5 spread makes a true blowout the flip, not the base, but a two-score lead is enough to trim fourth-quarter routes.
script.flip2: Chicago leads at home and Dallas is forced off the run. Javonte's 33-carry role shrinks, Sanders (9 carries, 68 yards, already had a 53-yard game) does not save a rush over, and Lamb, Pickens (13 targets, 152 air) and Ferguson targets rise. The other version of this flip is outdoor weather, which is not in the pack: wind 15+ or rain would cut Lamb's 12.6 aDOT and drag the 49.5 under, killing the pass overs together.

injury_fallout: Official pre-game nflverse injury report, known before kickoff. Final inactives (~90 minutes before kick) are not in the pack, so every snap assumption is pre-inactive. Chicago defense out: CB Jaylon Johnson (groin), CB Jaylon Jones (hamstring), slot CB Kyler Gordon (hamstring), LB T.J. Edwards (hamstring). LB D'Marco Jackson is Questionable (hamstring). That is three corners and the MIKE. Dallas pass-catchers face backups. Who gains: CeeDee Lamb, the primary target (24 of 80 tracked Dallas targets, 30 percent, 303 air yards), is the first beneficiary of Johnson being out; George Pickens (13 targets, 16 percent, 152 air) is the outside WR2 beneficiary; Jake Ferguson (18 targets, 22.5 percent, 112 air) is the beneficiary of Gordon (slot) and Edwards (LB) both being out, which is the skill's TE/slot/RB-receiving map. Javonte also gains a checkdown path (10 targets, 43 yards, minus-12 air) if Jackson sits, but his listed market edge is the run. Who loses on that side: no Dallas skill player is listed out, so nobody is absorbing a Dallas absence. Chicago offense: G Kiran Amegadjie Out (elbow) means pressure up, rush efficiency down, more quick throws, so Swift/Monangai rushing efficiency and Odunze deep yards are the losers, and short TE/RB catches (Kmet 6 targets / 60 yards, Swift 8 targets / 18 yards) are the gainers if Caleb gets sped up. RB D'Andre Swift Questionable (quadricep): if he is limited, Monangai is next man up. Monangai's share with Swift active has been 7 carries and 28 yards against Swift's 29 and 116, plus 4 targets and 19 yards. That is not a full role yet. Do not treat him as the starter until inactives. Dallas defense: CB DaRon Bland Out (foot). Who gains: Rome Odunze (20 of 64 tracked Chicago targets, 31 percent, 255 air) and, secondarily, DJ Moore (11 targets, 103 yards) and Olamide Zaccheaus (12 targets, 54 yards). No Dallas safety is listed out, so this is a corner absence, not a deep-safety absence.

matchup.shell: No MOFO/MOFC or man/zone charting was saved, so shell is inferred only from location splits and the injury report. Chicago, two games: YPA left 9.12 on 17 attempts, middle 13.9 on 10 attempts, right 8.71 on 21 attempts. The middle is the leak, on a small sample. Right is their least-bad side. With Johnson, Jones and Gordon all Out, any man matchup for Lamb or Pickens is a backup, and the slot (Gordon) is empty for Ferguson. Dallas, two games: left 7.23 on 31, middle 20.88 on 8, right 8.44 on 25. Dallas's middle number is uglier but it is 8 attempts, so it is a flag for fluke explosives, not a number to price an Odunze leg on. Bland being out is the real Chicago-receiver matchup fact.
matchup.pressure: Chicago blitz rate is 19 percent. Dak Prescott's EPA per dropback is 0.14 against the blitz and 0.10 with no blitz, so Chicago's pressure plan is not a problem for Dallas, and they rarely bring extra rushers. No Dallas offensive lineman is on the injury report, so time-to-throw should hold. That supports Lamb's air yards (303 on 24 targets) rather than killing deep yards and dumping everything to the back. Dallas blitzes 18 percent. Caleb Williams's EPA per dropback is minus-0.24 when blitzed and plus-0.12 when not. Dallas does not blitz enough to force the bad version of Caleb, which is why a Chicago pass over is not automatically dead, and also why it is not a pressure-driven edge. Chicago G Amegadjie being out is the pressure risk on the Chicago side, and it points at shorter throws, not at a Prescott problem.
matchup.bleeds: Chicago run defense has allowed 5.30 yards per carry and 9 runs of 10+ in two games. That is the clearest defensive bleed in the pack by play count. Chicago has also allowed 7 passes of 20+ on 51 attempts. Pass location bleed is the middle at 13.9 YPA, not the outside. Dallas run defense has allowed 4.38 YPC and 7 runs of 10+, a tighter front than Chicago's. Dallas has allowed 8 passes of 20+ on 68 attempts, with the middle at 20.88 YPA on only 8 throws. Do not treat that 20.88 as a stable scheme edge.
matchup.overlap: The core overlap is Lamb into the missing Chicago corners. He is the top option (24 targets, 222 yards, 303 air, both games 110 and 112) and Chicago is without the CB1 (Johnson), the slot corner (Gordon) and another corner (Jones), while also bleeding the middle. The second overlap is Ferguson into that same middle: 18 targets, short air (112 on 18, about 6.2 aDOT), Edwards out, Gordon out. Pickens overlaps the backup-corner fact (152 air yards) but not the middle bleed; Chicago's right side is 8.71 YPA, their best zone. Javonte overlaps the run bleed (5.30 YPC allowed vs his own 4.58 YPC on 33 carries) but that is a different script from the pass stack. Odunze overlaps Bland being out, not a charted weak safety, and the Dallas middle sample is too small to call it the same kind of overlap.

pre_mortem: It is Monday and this slip lost. Chicago, even without Johnson, Jones and Gordon, doubled Lamb with a safety and he finished in the same 110-112 band he has lived in for two weeks, so 111.5 never cleared. The explosives that the backups did give up went to Pickens, who had the 152 air yards, not to the tight end. Ferguson saw his targets and the 5.6 yards per target held: another afternoon in the 20s or 30s, because the 78 was the chunk-play game and the 13.9 middle YPA was a couple of explosives on only 10 attempts, not a weekly hole. Dallas also ran more than this pass stack needed, because Chicago had allowed 5.30 yards per carry and 9 runs of 10-plus, so Javonte's 33-carry role ate the plays Ferguson needed to reach 50.5. The Lamb counter is real but weaker than the read, because three corners out is a lot of bodies to replace while still bracketing a 24-target WR1 in a 49.5 game. The Ferguson counter is close to the read, which is why he is a lean. If inactives bring back a corner the report has as Out, or if wind is posted later, both legs should be re-run before any number is trusted.

Not in this slip: a total under, Odunze over 82.5 (Bland is out, but 37 and 128 straddle 82.5 and Amegadjie is out), Moore 51.5, Zaccheaus 27.5, or Monangai, who needs a Swift inactive that is not confirmed.
